**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity), Section 2.1 (p0012).**

What I checked and found:
- No express "liquidated damages" or penalty language anywhere in the body; searches for "liquidated damages", "penalt", and termination-for-convenience fees returned nothing adverse (the only "penalty" hit, 27.3, benefits us).
- Service credits are referenced only in the Fees definition (1.5) and run in our favour — compliant.
- The real exposure is **2.1's take-or-pay**: USD 2,000,000 per year for three years (USD 6,000,000) payable "without reduction or termination rights." That is a Customer-payable liquidated amount equal to the full remaining contract value, owed even for Services never consumed and even after we terminate for Cobalt's breach — squarely in the walk-away band. It also conflicts with 7.1 (no unstated minimum-use charge), 12.3 (Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment) and 27.3 (termination "without penalty").

Redline (validated ok:true): converts the binding minimum into a non-binding volume expectation, confirms we pay only for Services actually ordered, and states that no take-or-pay charge, shortfall, minimum fee, penalty, liquidated damages, or early-termination fee is payable by Customer, with reduction/termination rights preserved. The comment offers the playbook fallback of a single early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees.
